name: Gnetum-leaf soup
summary: A clear soup of lá bép, also called rau nhíp, which Go Vietnam groups with former Kon Tum as well as Gia Lai and Đắk Lắk. The shops that article names are in Pleiku and Buôn Ma Thuột.
origin: Go Vietnam calls canh lá bép a wild-vegetable soup of the Jrai, Ba Na, Xơ Đăng, and Ê Đê, most common in Gia Lai, the former Kon Tum area, and Đắk Lắk.
taste: Go Vietnam says lá bép gives a clean sweetness, a little crispness, and umami. Cooked, it is gently chewy and nutty. The soup is clear, sweet, and light.
howToEat: Wash the young shoots and tender leaves and simmer them. Go Vietnam says the leaf is sweet enough that the soup needs little seasoning. Eat it hot with rice, beside a stronger dish. The same article says communities also cook canh thụt, a separate tube.

A bowl price in Kon Tum was not printed. The article’s 2025 leaf prices are for highland markets, not a Kon Tum bowl: about 5,000–10,000 VND a bunch, and by weight about 59,000 VND a kilogram wholesale, 80,000–100,000 VND retail, and up to 120,000–200,000 VND at supermarkets. A bowl is Check on arrival. The rainy season, roughly May to October, is when it says the shoots are best.
where: The former Kon Tum area, on that article. The eateries it names are in Pleiku and Buôn Ma Thuột. A Kon Tum city address is Check on arrival.
